articles.title: How Long Should You Chase a Failed Payment?
articles.excerpt: Ask five subscription operators how long a dunning cycle should run and you will get five answers, each delivered with total confidence: three days, a week, two weeks, a month, until the next billing…
articles.body: Ask five subscription operators how long a dunning cycle should run and you will get five answers, each delivered with total confidence: three days, a week, two weeks, a month, until the next billing date. The confidence is the tell. Almost nobody derived their number from their own recovery data, because almost nobody has recovery data organized by day-since-failure. The number came from a default setting, a competitor's help doc, or a feeling that longer must mean pushier. Here is the measurement that settles it for your own book. Take the last two quarters of failed renewals that eventually recovered, and plot them by the day the money actually arrived.

articles.title: Your real investment return: writing XIRR from scratch in Python
articles.excerpt: Brokerage apps show a return number, but if you've been adding money at random times, a simple "gain divided by deposits" figure is misleading. The right tool is the money-weighted return, the same th…
articles.body: Brokerage apps show a return number, but if you've been adding money at random times, a simple "gain divided by deposits" figure is misleading. The right tool is the money-weighted return, the same thing spreadsheet users get from XIRR . Here's how it works and how to compute it yourself. The problem Say you deposited: $5,000 on Jan 1 $3,000 on Jul 1 $2,000 on Oct 1 and on Dec 31 the account is worth $10,900. You put in $10,000 and gained $900. Is that 9%? No. Most of the money wasn't invested for the whole year, so the annualized return is higher.

articles.title: Declare your color schemes before the first paint (Web HIG tip #17)
articles.excerpt: You open example.com on a phone that prefers dark mode. The page was authored as light, with no color-scheme in the head or the first CSS. In the Safari 27.3 beta, with Adaptive Dark Mode turned on, S…
articles.body: You open example.com on a phone that prefers dark mode. The page was authored as light, with no color-scheme in the head or the first CSS. In the Safari 27.3 beta, with Adaptive Dark Mode turned on, Safari can repaint that light page as dark: colors and light gradients change, some SVG images and simple logos recolor, and some masks or blend effects can be turned off. Scripts that read the page's colors still get the authored values. The page never told the browser which schemes it supports. Web HIG tip #17 (Quick #64): Dark mode must re-verify contrast for every semantic token combination used. Declare supported color schemes in the document head or the initial CSS, before JavaScript. light dark is the usual declaration when both schemes are supported.

articles.title: I counted every element in 11,176 slide renders: 0.54% got baked into images
articles.excerpt: When you turn HTML into a shape-based document like PPTX, anything you can't map to a shape or a text box ends up as a cropped screenshot. The user can't edit that picture as text, and it goes soft wh…
articles.body: When you turn HTML into a shape-based document like PPTX, anything you can't map to a shape or a text box ends up as a cropped screenshot. The user can't edit that picture as text, and it goes soft when zoomed. I wanted to know how much of my own converter's output is like that, so I counted. Short version: across 11,176 renders of my own slide layout library (254 layouts times 44 themes), there are 408,267 measured elements, and 2,200 of them (0.54%) become pictures. The list is identical in all 44 themes, so it is 50 elements per theme, in 12 layouts. What I measured and how A script opens each layout in headless Chromium at a fixed 1920x1080, walks the DOM, and writes one JSON file per (layout, theme) pair. Every element gets a kind: shape , text , svgShapes , arcs or decoration .

articles.title: One Vite build, two runtimes: shipping a browser game to the open web and into an offline WebView
articles.excerpt: I shipped ApexDrawn as a plain static site: you draw a closed loop, it becomes a racetrack, and then you drive it. Later I needed a second build target - a mobile shell that loads the same game from l…
articles.body: I shipped ApexDrawn as a plain static site: you draw a closed loop, it becomes a racetrack, and then you drive it. Later I needed a second build target - a mobile shell that loads the same game from local assets with no network at all. The interesting part wasn't the game logic. It was that the whole app assumed a server: accounts, /api/* for purchases and garage state, a WebSocket relay for races, analytics, payments. None of that can exist in an offline WebView. I didn't want a fork, so the split is one build-time flag and everything else follows from it. One flag, two bundles // src/appMode.ts export const OFFLINE_APP = import . meta . env . VITE_OFFLINE_APP === "true" ; Because this is a compile-time constant, Rollup tree-shakes the unreachable branch.

Before generating pages, map its chapters to customer questions, extract specifications and images, remove outdated information, and define a review process. 1. Why a PDF Manual Cannot Be Directly Turned into Website Pages PDF layout logic is print logic: columns, cross-page tables, headers and footers, and figure numbering. AI website builders need web logic: a page list, one topic per page, paragraphs, lists, and citable specification tables. The mapping between the two does not happen automatically.

articles.title: Checking domain availability, WHOIS and DNS from one API call
articles.excerpt: If you've ever built a domain search box, a brand-name generator or an internal "is this domain still ours?" check, you know the pattern: one provider for availability, another for WHOIS/RDAP, a DNS r…
articles.body: If you've ever built a domain search box, a brand-name generator or an internal "is this domain still ours?" check, you know the pattern: one provider for availability, another for WHOIS/RDAP, a DNS resolver library, and maybe an SSL checker on top. Each has its own auth, its own JSON shape and its own rate limits. I've been trying out DomSDK , a domain data API that puts these lookups behind a single key and a consistent JSON style. Here's a quick walkthrough of the calls I found most useful. 1. Availability curl "https://api.domsdk.com/v1/availability?domain=my-new-idea.com" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_KEY" The response is a small object with the domain, the TLD and an available boolean, which is all a search box really needs. 2.

articles.title: This supernova impostor baffled astronomers for 15 years — until they found a hidden black hole feeding on an unstable star
articles.excerpt: A hidden black hole or neutron star companion to an unstable massive star is causing the system to erupt in light that mimics a supernova explosion.
articles.body: A cosmic imposter that has faked being a supernova 27 times and counting is actually a hot, luminous, and decidedly unstable star that is being fed on by a vampiric black hole or neutron star, NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory has discovered. When a massive star reaches the end of the road and runs out of nuclear fuel to power fusion reactions in its core, the star is destroyed in a supernova explosion. That’s what astronomers thought they had found on 11 January 2012, when they observed what appeared to be a supernova on the outskirts of the spiral galaxy NGC 4559, which is about 25 million light-years away in the constellation Coma Berenices. Yet when the light of the 'supernova' faded, the star was still there, only to continue bursting into light every 113 days.

articles.title: Nvidia privately confirmed it could track chips to fight smuggling, even as industry publicly questioned feasibility
articles.excerpt: Representatives from Nvidia told Illinois representative Bill Foster that it would be technically possible to implement the anti-smuggling measures called for in the Chip Security Act, Foster told MIT…
articles.body: Representatives from Nvidia told Illinois representative Bill Foster that it would be technically possible to implement the anti-smuggling measures called for in the Chip Security Act, Foster told MIT Technology Review in an interview on Thursday, even while an industry group claimed they were “potentially infeasible.” Foster, a Democrat who serves on the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, is a cosponsor of the act, which would introduce geotracking requirements to verify the location of advanced AI chips in order to prevent their smuggling to China.
